problems.problem: Let $n>k>0$ be integers. A leader secretly gives a deputy an $n$-bit string. The deputy lists every string differing from it in exactly $k$ positions. A contestant sees this list. Determine the minimum guesses guaranteeing identification of the secret string.

Triangle $ABC$ has circumcircle $\Gamma$, incentre $I$ and midpoint $M$ of $BC$. Points $D\in BC,E\in CA,F\in AB$ satisfy $ID\perp BC,IE\perp AI,IF\perp AI$. Circle $AEF$ meets $\Gamma$ again at $X\ne A$. Prove that $XD$ and $AM$ intersect on $\Gamma$.

Circles $G_1,G_2$ intersect at $M,N$. A common tangent touches them at $A,B$, nearer $M$ than $N$. Through $M$, a parallel meets them at $C,D$. Set $E=AC\cap BD$, $P=AN\cap CD$, $Q=BN\cap CD$. Prove $EP=EQ$ and that $EN$ bisects $\angle CND$.
For $\gcd(n,6)=1$, colour a regular $n$-gon with three colours, each used an odd number of times. Prove that some isosceles triangle has vertices of different colours.
Write $S(k)$ for the decimal digit sum. Determine $P\in\mathbb Z[x]$ satisfying $P(n)>0$ and $S(P(n))=P(S(n))$ for every integer $n\ge2016$.
